text.p: Retailer Woolworths Ltd said on Tuesday its Christmas sales had exceeded expectations, with a strong performance across all trading groups.
Woolworths earlier reported first half sales to January 5, 1997 of A$8.22 billion, up 8.61 percent on the previous corresponding half.
"Christmas, finally, over the last three or four days, exceeded our expectations," chief executive officer Reg Clairs told Reuters.
"Like all retailers we had our heart in our mouth as we worked through December, but those last few days...in the supermarkets in particular, were extraordinarily strong in fresh foods," he said.
"In the meantime, we had had a very good last week with the (general merchandise) Big W stores," he said.

On a "like for like" or comparable stores basis, sales rose 3.77 percent, Woolworths said. First half food sales were up 8.60 percent, general merchandise up 9.50 percent and specialty retail up 4.92 percent.
Asked about the impact on the first half profit result, Clairs said: "It would appear it's going to be a satisfactory result, but I can't really predict that until all the numbers are in."
A number Australian retailers have issued profit warnings for the half-year to January in recent weeks following disappointing Christmas sales.
The retailer had been able to maintain sales growth by adjusting its product range in line with the changing needs of consumers, he said.
Supermarkets were stocking more semi-prepared and fully-prepared food for time-poor customers, while in apparel, more casual clothes were being offered at cheaper prices.
Clairs said high levels of unemployment, job insecurity and changing patterns of disposable income meant more people were prepared to buy clothes from a discount department store.

This included people who might be spending a greater proportion of their income than previously on holidays, sports or computers than previously. Clairs said Woolworths hoped to maintain sales growth in the second half of "8.0 to 8.5 percent". -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
